sentences.text: Gryphoceratops was an extinct ceratopsian dinosaur belonging to the family Leptoceratopsidae, found in Alberta, southern Canada.
The holotype likely represents the smallest known adult ceratopsian from North America.
Despite being the oldest known leptoceratopsid, a cladistic analysis suggests it was one of the most advanced members of the group.
The only known fossil of Gryphoceratops is a partial right dentary bone designated as holotype ROM 56635.
The holotype was discovered in bonebed 55 of the Milk River Formation within Dinosaur Provincial Park, dating to approximately 83 million years ago.
The genus Gryphoceratops was first named by Michael J. Ryan, David C. Evans, Philip J. Currie, Caleb M. Brown, and Don Brinkman in 2012.
Gryphoceratops is considered the oldest-known member of the leptoceratopsid family.
Gryphoceratops lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago.
